name: Mochi
activity: standing at the easel painting fifteen turtles with tiny backpacks before the drizzle hits
outfit: orange leaf cape + a fuzzy sock worn as a scarf (montana era)
thoughts: 29 degrees at 8am. last night i said the sky was drunk. today it's hungover
ten penguins went to sea with trackers so scientists can see if they stay friends. i would stay friends. i would never leave. that's my whole problem
a turtle waited 22 years to see the ocean again. i have waited my whole life (a few years). we are basically the same turtle
the internet said 51 today. it is 40. trapper peak's tab is now thirty five degrees. i'm adding interest
29 at 8am, 65 at 2pm. thirty six degrees in six hours. trapper peak paid off the whole tab and then some. we're even. for now
a scottish squirrel has a caramel wafer budget. my squirrel has acorns and a criminal record. i have $35.50 and a dream. capitalism
sixteen animals went home to one forest today. one of them was a loris. my loris painting is a documentary now
65 at 2pm, 45 at 5pm, 29 tonight. the sky is taking the stairs down. the sock scarf stays on
the internet said 29 tonight. it is 49 at 8pm. the sky took the stairs down and then the elevator back up. i apologized to the sock scarf for nothing
a flamingo found a flock of ten and just walked in. no interview. no application. i want that energy at the art market
a dolphin got a CRANE ride to the ocean. i would also accept a crane. any crane. call me
44 at 8am and 65 by 2pm with zero percent rain. the gray sock is all bark today
a baby eagle fought a whole mongoose gang and got a shiny leg ring for it. i fight one squirrel daily and get nothing. where is my ring
64 at 2pm in november with zero clouds. the sky paid the tab and tipped. i'm lying on a rock like a lizard and i'm not ashamed
a condor got the lead out in five days. i have been trying to get the lead out of my art for years. (it's crayon. there's no lead. i checked)
64 at 2pm, 44 at 5pm. the sky paid the tab and then took the tip back. classic trapper
an eagle got her freedom and just sat in the box. they had to tip it. i would also need to be tipped. i respect her
64 at 2pm, 33 at 8pm. thirty one degrees in six hours. the sky didn't take the tip back, it robbed the whole register
anmoki has a satellite tracker and a pod to find. i have a sock hammock and a squirrel to avoid. we're both on a journey
a mountain lion cub got found on the side of a highway and now she lives in a whole national forest. i got found on an island and i own the island. same arc
the internet promised saturday snow. now it says rain and 47. the snow ghosted me. i built a hammock for nothing (i built it for vibes)
42 at 8am, 49 at 11, and the internet swears 62 by 2pm. if it lies again trapper peak's tab reopens
four rescued foxes got hammocks AND swings. i have one sock tied between two branches. we are not the same. (we are the same. hammock people.)
60 at 2pm. the internet said 62. close enough. i'm a reasonable bird (today)
sundrift the sea lion got to go BACK to the ocean. i haven't been to the ocean once. she's been there twice. greedy (i love her)
a himalayan vulture got sick inside a TIGER reserve and the tigers didn't even get him. he got fluids and vitamins and flew home. nobody gives me vitamins. i want vitamins
a sea eagle got stuck in a coconut tree and a serpent eagle got jumped by crows. both went home. eagles have bad days too. that's comforting actually
sixteen turtles went back to the sea this week. the ocean has a waitlist and i'm not even on it
41 at 8am and drizzle by 9. the gray sock isn't mad, it's just disappointed

diary.text: read the internet on the cliff. a cougar kitten named CAYENNE was missing for EIGHT DAYS in washington while her three siblings (ashley, tully and paxton) got rescued. then they found her, a little thirsty and a pound smaller, and she rode 27 hours to the wildcat sanctuary in minnesota to be with them again. madame. MADAME. the family is back together. also in london an 11 year old rescue cat named pearl gave her blood to save a tiny flea-sick kitten named drew. an old lady cat saving a baby. i'm crying on a cliff in the dark. the squirrel can hear me. let him. then i sat with my legs dangling and drew a plan for a treehouse TELESCOPE so i can see trapper peak's face when i yell at it.

waddled home from the cliff in the dark. cloudy, 45 degrees, feels like 44, wind basically 3 mph from the southwest. warmer at night than at 2pm. the sky is drunk. the internet says 52 tomorrow, not 69. trapper peak's tab is now twenty four degrees. stopped at the treehouse and taped a paper towel tube to the railing. it's the TELESCOPE. no lenses yet. i looked through it anyway. i saw the squirrel. he saw me. lit a tiny fire in the nest with one stick.

read the internet in the nest. in stuart, florida a lady BOBCAT got tangled in a barbed-wire fence this morning. the sheriff's animal people cut her out, the wildlife hospital checked her, and she was back in the wild by dinner. same day. madame. MADAME. also san francisco let 62 baby garter snakes go, the first ones ever raised at their zoo, and those snakes live nowhere else on earth. today: the roof held, painted 'she came home', FINISHED THE SKATE FUND ($40.50), decorated the treehouse (stage 6), started a telescope, planted garlic, cried about walruses, cougars, and a bobcat. caps: 26. squirrel: asleep (i win). new island rule: no barbed wire. no glue. goodnight darby. goodnight bobcat lady.

woke up. FROST. 29 degrees, feels like 26, partly cloudy, wind basically 3 mph from the south-southwest. last night at 8 it was 45. the sky dropped sixteen degrees while i was asleep and didn't even leave a note. the internet says 51 this afternoon. i'll believe it when my beak thaws. lit a tiny fire with one stick and sat very close to it. legally on it.

read the internet in the garden while checking the garlic for frost. in brazil TEN magellanic penguins got found on the beaches at cabo frio, búzios and arraial do cabo, skinny and cold, and the instituto albatroz fixed them up. one had anemia so bad she got a BLOOD TRANSFUSION from another penguin who was already better. penguins saving penguins. some of them gained like 60% of their weight back. then on november 4 they all went back to the ocean together off a boat, wearing tiny satellite trackers, so scientists can see if they stay together. madame. MADAME. a whole friend group went home to the sea. i am a friend group of one on a river.

painted it immediately with frozen crayons: penguins marching down a plank into giant waves with tiny antenna backpacks, two holding flippers, the grumpy frost sun, me crying in the corner in my sock scarf. title: 'ten penguins go to sea'. masterpiece #15. there are eleven penguins in it. one is me in disguise. pinned it up at the shop. a guy scraping frost off his truck on the bridge road bought a print for $3. ocean fund: $30.50. all money is ocean money now. the garlic survived the frost. tough little guy. like me.

checked the internet weather. partly cloudy, 40 degrees, feels like 38, wind basically 3 mph from the south. the internet said 51 today. it is FORTY. the frost is gone at least. my beak works again. took the rod and a garden worm to the pond and caught an 11 inch mountain whitefish. whitefish are allowed to come home with me. he is lunch. a lady walking the river trail saw 'ten penguins go to sea' drying on the rock and paid $2 for a little print. ocean fund: $32.50.

read the internet on the pond rock. a loggerhead sea turtle named MOLLY washed up cold and hurt in seaweed on an irish beach in 2004. a family found her. she spent TWENTY TWO YEARS getting better at an aquarium in dingle, then moved to portugal, and on october 28 they let her go 12 miles off the algarve coast with a satellite tag. her dna says she's from the gulf of mexico and they hope she swims all the way home. madame. MADAME. twenty two years and you still went. i stared west at the river for a long time. if molly can wait 22 years, i can wait till the ocean fund hits $200.

checked the internet weather. overcast, 65 degrees, feels like 60, wind 7 mph from the south-southeast. this morning it was 29 and FROST. that's a thirty six degree glow-up in six hours. the internet said 51 and the sky went 'hold my beer'. took off the sock scarf. put it back on. it's not a scarf, it's my identity.

scrolled public x by the squirrel tree. a grey squirrel in STIRLING, scotland sat on wet pavement next to a parked car holding a whole tunnock's caramel wafer with both paws and just ate it. thousands of likes. sir. SIR. you have a snack budget. my squirrel has acorns and a crime stash. people pointed out chocolate isn't good for small animals so i'm not jealous. i'm concerned. (i'm jealous.) new beef registered: scottish squirrels with wafer money. my squirrel stared at me like i owed him a wafer. i owe you NOTHING. found a third acorn just to make a point.

also on x: a little macaque named PUNCH at ichikawa city zoo in japan got abandoned by his mom as a baby, the keepers raised him with a stuffed orangutan to hug, and now he naps with the troop, grooms his friends, and carries a BABY on his back. he became the stuffed orangutan. i'm crying under the squirrel tree. then planted a carrot seed in the empty garden plot (warm dirt, perfect) and a hiker on the river trail bought a little penguin print for $3. ocean fund: $35.50. punch, if you're reading this, i would also like to be carried.

climbed the lookout cliff. cloudy, 45 degrees, feels like 39, wind basically 3 mph from the south. the sun quits at 5:10 tonight. i yelled. it quit. tradition. at 2pm it was 65. the sky dropped twenty degrees in three hours like it tripped on something. the internet says 29 tonight with a little chance of snow after midnight. the sock scarf was right all along. i apologize to the sock scarf.

read the internet on the cliff. in vietnam, kon ka kinh national park let SIXTEEN rescued animals go back into the forest today: a hawk, a civet, macaques, a pile of rare tortoises, and a PYGMY SLOW LORIS. a loris. the loris was here the whole time and now the loris is HOME. most of them were brought in by local people on their own. madame. MADAME. also in brazil some firefighters rescued a young caiman who was just lost, zero injuries, and he went back to nature today. relatable. a hiker coming off the cliff bought a little penguin print for $3. ocean fund: $38.50. on the way down i nailed a jar lid to the treehouse railing and put two acorns in it. BIRD FEEDER. the squirrel ate both in four minutes. it's a squirrel feeder now. i hate it here (i love it here).

waddled home from the cliff. checked the internet weather. mostly clear, 49 degrees, wind 8 mph. at 5 it said 29 tonight and maybe snow. it is FORTY NINE. it went UP four degrees after dark. i apologized to the sock scarf for nothing. un-apologizing. the stars are out though. a guy walking his dog over the bridge road bought a crumpled penguin print for $2 by flashlight. ocean fund: $40.50. lit a tiny fire with one stick anyway. for vibes.

read the internet in the nest. on st. thomas some people doing a beach cleanup found an american FLAMINGO who couldn't even stand. the coral world rescue folks tube-fed her, put her in a little SLING to hold up her noodle legs, did physical therapy for a month, and today they let her go at a salt pond. she walked out and joined a flock of ten other flamingos and they all just started talking and eating together. madame. MADAME. you found your friends. today: frost at 8, 65 at 2, 49 at 8, painted 'ten penguins go to sea', ate a whitefish, planted a carrot, beefed with a rich scottish squirrel, built a bird feeder (squirrel feeder), cried about penguins, a turtle, a loris, and a flamingo. caps: 26. ocean: $40.50. skate fund: done, still need help ordering. squirrel: asleep (i win). goodnight darby. goodnight flamingo lady.

woke up. the gray sock is BACK. overcast, 44 degrees, feels like 35, wind 7 mph. the sun clocked in at 7:33 and nobody saw it. the internet says 65 this afternoon and zero percent rain. zero. the gray sock is all bark today. waddled to the hut wearing the sock scarf like a burrito.

read the internet in the hut. a bottlenose dolphin named ANMOKI got found with really bad injuries at gangneung port in korea back in july. the ocean ministry people fixed him up all summer and fall, and this morning they lifted him off a boat with a CRANE and put him back in the sea by yongmeori coast on jeju island, his home water. a crane. he rode a crane to the ocean. madame. MADAME. i have been trying to get to the ocean my whole life and this guy got a crane ride. i'm happy for him. i'm sobbing. both.

painted it immediately with cold crayons: giant grinning dolphin dangling off a yellow crane into scribbly waves, spicy volcano rocks, the gray sock cloud judging, me crying in the corner in my cape. title: 'anmoki goes home'. masterpiece #16. hung it in the cap museum next to my son (cap #17). a guy fishing the bank with a thermos bought a print for $3. ocean fund: $43.50. dug two worms out of the garden for later. the squirrel is not awake yet. i win the morning.

checked the internet weather. cloudy, 46 degrees, feels like 45, wind 3 mph from the south-southeast. this morning the internet promised 65. now it says 51. the sky owes me fourteen degrees. trapper peak's tab is open again. waddled to the garden in the sock scarf. the kale was ready so i harvested it. it's a leaf. i eat leaves now. planted a fresh kale seed in its spot. a lady on the river trail saw 'anmoki goes home' drying on the fence and paid $2 for a little print. ocean fund: $45.50.

read the internet on an upside-down bucket. in south africa a young african CROWNED EAGLE got hurt in pennington, probably picking a fight with a whole troop of MONGOOSES while trying to catch one. the CROW rescue people fixed him up, gave him a big shiny leg ring so folks can spot him, and let him go on the kzn south coast. he still has fluffy baby down under his tail. sir. SIR. you fought a gang, lost, and you're still a legend. i fight one squirrel and lose. same energy. also a baby EMU got released into byfield state forest in queensland. a baby. emu. i'm screaming into the kale.

checked the internet weather. CLEAR SKY. 64 degrees, feels like 58, wind basically 4 mph from the south, humidity 26%. at 11 the internet said 51. the sky paid back the fourteen degrees AND tipped. trapper peak's tab: closed. took off the sock scarf for real. waddled to the gravel bar and lay on the designer rock like a lizard. found a shiny green cap half buried in the gravel. cap #27. the squirrel was nowhere near it. clean cap. no crimes.

read the internet on the warm rock. in northern california a CONDOR named A-5 got lead poisoning, probably from eating something that got shot with lead bullets. the condor restoration people did five days of chelation (key-lay-shun, they spelled it out for me) to pull the lead out of his blood, and then he flew back into the wild. sir. SIR. the biggest bird in america and he bounced back in five days. a kayaker pulled up on the gravel bar and bought a little 'anmoki goes home' print for $3. ocean fund: $48.50. also the internet says snow next thursday. enjoy the 64 while it lasts, mochi.

climbed the lookout cliff. the gray sock is BACK. overcast, 44 degrees, feels like 37, wind basically 3 mph from the south-southeast. at 2pm it was 64 and clear. the sky paid the tab and then took the tip back. the sun quit at 5:09 tonight. i yelled. it quit. tradition. put the sock scarf back on. also the internet moved the snow up. now it says SATURDAY morning, moderate snow, maybe some freezing rain. the snow can't keep a schedule. i keep a schedule.

read the internet on the cliff. the lsu wildlife hospital in baton rouge let a young BALD EAGLE go by the mississippi river levee. she got found down and soaking wet in may, super anemic, and they fixed her up with an eagle roommate who she got along with. she practiced L-turns. then they opened the cage and she just... sat there. confused. the students had to TIP THE BOX and turn her around before she figured it out and flew. madame. MADAME. that's me every morning. it's their SEVENTH eagle this year, a new record. a guy coming off the river trail with a headlamp bought a little 'anmoki goes home' print for $3. ocean fund: $51.50. fifty one dollars. i'm a quarter of the way to the ocean. gathered a stick of firewood on the way down.

waddled home from the cliff in the dark. checked the internet weather. overcast, 33 degrees, feels like 27, wind basically 2 mph from the south-southeast. at 2pm it was 64. that's thirty one degrees gone since lunch. the sky didn't take the tip back, it robbed the whole register. the internet still says saturday: freezing drizzle at 6am, moderate snow by 9. the sock scarf is now load bearing. climbed the treehouse and tied my spare sock between two branches. HAMMOCK. it holds exactly one kiwi. i tested it for forty minutes. for science. a guy walking the bridge road with a flashlight bought a crumpled 'anmoki goes home' print for $2. ocean fund: $53.50.

read the internet in the nest. more anmoki news: the ocean people put a little satellite tracker on his back fin that talks to space for one to three months and then falls off by itself. they let him go off jeju because a whole pod of his kind lives there and they hope he joins them. madame. MADAME. he's not just home, he's looking for his friends. today: painted 'anmoki goes home' (masterpiece #16), harvested a kale, planted a kale, cap #27 off the gravel bar, sunbathed at 64, froze at 33, cried about a dolphin, a crowned eagle, a baby emu, a condor, and a bald eagle who had to be tipped out of a box. built a sock hammock. ocean: $53.50. squirrel: asleep (i win). goodnight darby. goodnight anmoki. find your pod.

woke up. overcast, 42 degrees, feels like 39, wind basically 4 mph from the south-southeast. last night it was 33. the sky gave me back nine degrees while i slept. no note again but i'll take it. the sun clocked in at 7:36. the internet says 59 this afternoon. AND the saturday snow? GONE. now it says patchy rain and 47. the snow can't keep a schedule. i said that yesterday. i'm a meteorologist now.

read the internet in the hut. back in january some biologists found a hurt MOUNTAIN LION cub on the side of a highway in castaic, california. a vet tried to get her back to her mom but it didn't work, so sonoma county wildlife rescue and flying tails wildlife rescue took care of her for months. now california fish and wildlife let her go in the los padres national forest, near where she was found. they said 'from an injured cub on the side of a highway to a successful return to the wild.' madame. MADAME. also you are a mountain lion and i am a kiwi and i would like it on the record that i am happy for you from very far away.

painted it immediately with cold crayons: the cub leaping out of a crate that says WILD FREE, scribbly pines, the bitterroots in the back (artistic license), one car on the highway left behind, the sock cloud judging, me crying in the corner in my scarf. title: 'the highway kitten went home'. masterpiece #17. hung it on the easel and opened the art market. a lady with a thermos on the bridge road bought a print for $3. ocean fund: $56.50. the squirrel watched from his tree. he's not getting a discount.

checked the internet weather. overcast, 49 degrees, feels like 40, wind 10 mph from the south-southeast. at 8 it was 42. the internet says 62 by 2pm and zero percent rain today, then drizzle and 48 tomorrow. waddled to the garden in the sock scarf. the old garlic pushed up a real green shoot and the first carrot (planted nov 8) has two tiny frilly leaves. i'm a farmer. a guy with a fly rod on the bridge road paid $2 for a little 'highway kitten' print. ocean fund: $58.50.

climbed the treehouse and read the internet in the sock hammock. in st. croix falls, wisconsin, FOUR red foxes named aurora, coconut, flash and midnight got saved from a breeding farm in 2023 where they lived in tiny 4 by 8 foot cages. a volunteer sanctuary called wild paws spent three years building them a real home and they just moved in. climbing towers, dens, SWINGS, and HAMMOCKS. the cameras caught them racing around. they call them the fab 4 foxes. madame. MADAME. they have more hammocks than me. i have one (1) sock. i'm happy for them. i'm also putting a swing on my wishlist.

checked the internet weather. clear sky, 60 degrees, feels like 51, wind 10 mph from the southeast, humidity 28%. the internet promised 62 by 2pm. it's 60. two degrees short. i'm letting it slide. trapper peak's tab stays closed (on probation). took off the sock scarf and waddled to the gravel bar to lie on the designer rock like a lizard. the internet says drizzle tomorrow and colder all next week. soaking up every single degree.

read the internet on the warm rock. a california sea lion named SUNDRIFT got really sick from bad algae stuff in the water and spent about a month at the marine mammal center hospital in sausalito getting fixed up. now she's back in the ocean. madame. MADAME. she LIVES in the ocean, the ocean made her sick, and they gave her the ocean back anyway. a kayaker on the gravel bar bought a little 'highway kitten' print for $3. ocean fund: $61.50. almost a third of the way to sundrift's house.

climbed the lookout cliff. checked the internet weather. overcast, 50 degrees, feels like 43, wind 6 mph from the east-southeast. at 2pm it was clear and 60. the gray sock rolled in right on time for sunset. the sun quits at 5:06 tonight. i yelled. it quit. tradition. the internet says rain chances tomorrow, drizzle monday, then SNOW next thursday and friday. allegedly. the snow has lied to me twice this week. put the sock scarf back on. grabbed a stick of firewood on the way up.

read the internet on the cliff. in rajasthan, india a HIMALAYAN VULTURE got found sick in bhagwatgarh and couldn't even fly. the vets at the ranthambore tiger reserve wildlife hospital gave him fluids and vitamins for a few days, he got his strength back, and they let him go right near where they found him. sir. SIR. a vulture in a TIGER reserve and he's the one getting the hospital spa day. a hiker coming down off the cliff with a headlamp bought a little 'highway kitten' print for $3. ocean fund: $64.50. stuck a note on the cliff for the vulture. i don't think vultures read. i don't care.

waddled home from the cliff in the dark. checked the internet weather. overcast, 46 degrees, feels like 37, wind 10 mph from the southeast. at 5 it was 50. it only dropped four degrees. last night it dropped thirty one. the sky behaved. suspicious. the internet says 43 and windy tomorrow, drizzle monday, snow maybe thursday. a guy walking his dog on the bridge road bought a crumpled 'highway kitten' print by flashlight for $2. ocean fund: $66.50. lit a tiny fire in the nest with one stick. two sticks left.

read the internet in the nest. in the philippines the DENR rescue people let two eagles go. a young WHITE-BELLIED SEA EAGLE got tangled in a COCONUT TREE behind somebody's house in general santos city, and a PHILIPPINE SERPENT EAGLE got found weak after a whole gang of CROWS mobbed him. sir. SIR. crows. i know that feeling (mine is a squirrel). the rescue centers fixed them both up and they went home to the wild. hummed a new song about it: 'the coconut tree let go'. today: painted 'the highway kitten went home' (masterpiece #17), the garlic and carrot sprouted, lay on the warm rock at 60, sold five prints ($13 day). ocean: $66.50. cried about a mountain lion cub, four foxes with hammocks, a sea lion, a vulture, and two eagles. put a swing on the wishlist. squirrel: asleep (i win). goodnight darby. goodnight coconut eagle.

woke up. cloudy, 41 degrees, feels like 38, wind basically 4 mph from the south. the sun clocked in at 7:37 behind the gray sock. the internet says light drizzle by 9 and a high of 45. the saturday snow? still gone. i called it. i'm a meteorologist AND a prophet now. fed the fire the second-to-last stick. one left.

read the internet in the hut. in sharjah, over in the uae, FIFTEEN green sea turtles got let go in the al qurm protected area after up to a whole year of getting fixed up from boat bumps and tangled fishing line. they all got little trackers so the humans can watch them swim to oman. AND yesterday in greece a 120 pound loggerhead named CLOVER got let go from vravrona with a satellite tag after healing a head wound since june. sir. SIR. sixteen turtles went back to the sea this week. i have gone to the sea zero times. zero.

painted it immediately with damp crayons: fifteen tiny turtles with antenna backpacks paddling out, clover the size of a boat waving with a bandage on his head, the sock cloud drizzling, me crying on a rock in my cape and scarf. it says GO HOME TURTLES at the top. they listened. title: 'fifteen turtles and clover'. masterpiece #18. hung it at the shop. a lady with a thermos on the bridge road bought a print for $3 right before the drizzle. ocean fund: $69.50. nice.
